regions.name: Wood(s)
regions.description: A forested area or woodland.

regions.name: Desert
regions.description: A barren, sandy, or rocky arid biome.

regions.name: Delta
regions.description: A landform created by deposition of sediment at the mouth of a river.

regions.name: Mountain(s)
regions.description: Large natural elevations of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.

regions.name: Hill(s)
regions.description: Naturally raised areas of land, not as high or craggy as a mountain.

regions.name: Canyon(s)
regions.description: Deep clefts between cliffs or escarpments, often carved by a river.

regions.name: Basin
regions.description: A depression, or dip, in the Earth’s surface, often containing water or salt deposits.

regions.name: Glacier
regions.description: A slowly moving mass or river of ice formed by the accumulation and compaction of snow.

regions.name: Rainforest
regions.description: A luxuriant, dense forest rich in biodiversity, found in typically tropical areas with heavy rainfall.

regions.name: Fields
regions.description: Expansive areas of open land, often used for cultivation or pasture.

regions.name: Valley
regions.description: A low area of land between hills or mountains, typically with a river or stream flowing through it.

regions.name: Port
regions.description: A maritime facility where ships may dock to load and unload passengers and cargo.

regions.name: Plain
regions.description: A broad area of relatively flat land.

regions.name: Barren
regions.description: Land that is too poor to produce much or any vegetation.

regions.name: City
regions.description: A large human settlement, often center of commerce and culture.

regions.name: Lake
regions.description: A large body of water surrounded by land.

regions.name: Cliff(s)
regions.description: A steep rock face, especially at the edge of the sea.

regions.name: Island(s)
regions.description: A piece of land surrounded by water.

regions.name: Forest
regions.description: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.

regions.name: Jungle
regions.description: An area of land overgrown with dense forest and tangled vegetation, typically in the tropics.

regions.name: River
regions.description: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another such stream.

regions.name: Marsh
regions.description: An area of low-lying land that is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

regions.name: Road
regions.description: A wide way leading from one place to another, especially one with a specially prepared surface.

regions.name: Bayou
regions.description: A marshy outlet of a lake or river, typically found in flat, low-lying areas.

regions.name: Wasteland
regions.description: An unused area of land that has become barren or desolated.

regions.name: Moraine
regions.description: A mass of rocks and sediment carried down and deposited by a glacier.

regions.name: Swamp
regions.description: An area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

regions.name: Grassland
regions.description: A large open area of country covered with grass, especially one used for grazing.

regions.name: Scree
regions.description: A mass of small loose stones that form or cover a slope on a mountain.

landmarks.name: Workshop
landmarks.description: A place where things are crafted or repaired.

landmarks.name: Waterfall
landmarks.description: A cascade of water falling from a height.

landmarks.name: Wall
landmarks.description: A continuous vertical brick or stone structure that encloses or divides an area.

landmarks.name: Rock
landmarks.description: A large natural formed mass of stone.

landmarks.name: Stream
landmarks.description: A small, narrow river.

landmarks.name: Vineyard
landmarks.description: A plantation of grapevines, typically for winemaking.

landmarks.name: Caldera
landmarks.description: A large volcanic crater, typically one formed by a major eruption.

landmarks.name: Pool
landmarks.description: A small area of still water.

landmarks.name: Garden
landmarks.description: A piece of ground adjoined to a house, used for growing flowers, fruit, or vegetables.

landmarks.name: Village
landmarks.description: A group of houses and associated buildings, larger than a hamlet and smaller than a town.

landmarks.name: Trail
landmarks.description: A beaten path through the countryside.

landmarks.name: Tower
landmarks.description: A tall, narrow building, either freestanding or forming part of a larger structure.

landmarks.name: Settlement
landmarks.description: A place, typically one previously uninhabited, where people establish a community.

landmarks.name: Beach
landmarks.description: A pebbly or sandy shore, especially by the ocean.

landmarks.name: Town
landmarks.description: An urban area that has a name, defined boundaries, and local government.

landmarks.name: Stone
landmarks.description: A hard solid non-metallic mineral matter of which rock is made.

landmarks.name: Peak
landmarks.description: The pointed top of a mountain.

landmarks.name: Street
landmarks.description: A public road in a city or town, typically with houses and buildings on one or both sides.

landmarks.name: Mine
landmarks.description: An excavation in the earth for extracting coal or other minerals.

landmarks.name: Cave
landmarks.description: A natural underground chamber in a hillside or cliff.

landmarks.name: Path
landmarks.description: A way or track laid down for walking or made by continual treading.

landmarks.name: Library
landmarks.description: A building or room containing collections of books and periodicals.

landmarks.name: Hotel
landmarks.description: An establishment providing accommodation, meals, and other services for travelers.

landmarks.name: Quarry
landmarks.description: A place, typically a large, deep pit, from which stone or other materials are extracted.

landmarks.name: Crossing
landmarks.description: A place where two roads, tracks, or paths intersect.

landmarks.name: Graveyard
landmarks.description: A burial ground; a cemetery.

landmarks.name: Tunnel
landmarks.description: An artificial underground passage, especially one built through a hill or under a building.

landmarks.name: Pond
landmarks.description: A small body of still water formed naturally or by hollowing or embanking.

landmarks.name: Gate
landmarks.description: A hinged barrier used to close an opening in a wall, fence, or hedge.

landmarks.name: Dam
landmarks.description: A barrier constructed to hold back water and raise its level.

landmarks.name: Gorge
landmarks.description: A narrow valley between hills or mountains, typically with steep rocky walls and a stream running through it.

landmarks.name: Plateau
landmarks.description: An area of relatively level high ground.

landmarks.name: Volcano
landmarks.description: A mountain or hill having a crater or vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are being or have been erupted from the earth's crust.

landmarks.name: Meadow
landmarks.description: A piece of grassland, especially one used for hay.

landmarks.name: Pasture
landmarks.description: Land covered with grass and other low plants suitable for grazing animals, especially cattle or sheep.

landmarks.name: Camp
landmarks.description: A place with temporary accommodation of huts, tents, or other structures.

landmarks.name: Sanctuary
landmarks.description: A holy place; a temple or church, or a place of refuge and safety.

landmarks.name: Bog
landmarks.description: Wet muddy ground too soft to support a heavy body.

landmarks.name: Slope
landmarks.description: A surface of which one end or side is at a higher level than another; a rising or falling ground.

landmarks.name: Statue
landmarks.description: A carved or cast figure of a person or animal, especially one that is life-size or larger.

landmarks.name: Stadium
landmarks.description: A large built-up structure with tiers of seats for spectators at sporting events.

landmarks.name: Sea
landmarks.description: The expanse of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface and surrounds its landmasses.

landmarks.name: Mound
landmarks.description: A rounded mass of projecting earth or stone, often artificial.

landmarks.name: Palace
landmarks.description: A large and impressive building forming the official residence of a ruler or dignitary.

landmarks.name: Dump
landmarks.description: A site for depositing garbage or waste material.

landmarks.name: Coast
landmarks.description: The part of the land adjoining or near the sea.

landmarks.name: Thicket
landmarks.description: A dense group of bushes or trees.

landmarks.name: Maze
landmarks.description: A network of paths and hedges designed as a puzzle through which one has to find a way.

landmarks.name: Plaza
landmarks.description: A public square, marketplace, or similar open space in a built-up area.

landmarks.name: Bay
landmarks.description: A broad inlet of the sea where the land curves inward.

landmarks.name: Clearing
landmarks.description: An open space in a forest, especially one cleared for cultivation.

landmarks.name: Floodplain
landmarks.description: An area of low-lying ground adjacent to a river, formed mainly of river sediments and subject to flooding.

landmarks.name: Glade
landmarks.description: An open space in a forest.

landmarks.name: Crossroad
landmarks.description: A road that crosses another road; an intersection.

landmarks.name: Restaurant
landmarks.description: A place where people pay to sit and eat meals that are cooked and served on the premises.
